sources.title: Medium is the new large.
sources.evidence: The May 7, 2025 announcement names Mistral Medium 3, describes coding and multimodal understanding, and states that its API is available that day. Enterprise deployment and customization require contacting Mistral. It supplies no production parameter count or architecture specification.

sources.title: Mistral Medium 3 — Mistral Docs
sources.evidence: Exact v25.05 card maps Mistral Medium 3 to mistral-medium-2505, dates it May 7, 2025, labels it Premier, advertises 128k context, and lists function calling and chat completions. It is a deprecated historical card; its displayed replacement is Medium 3.5.

sources.title: Mistral Docs published model definitions, exact Medium 3 v25.05 entry
sources.evidence: Public script loaded by the exact model page declares slug mistral-medium-3-25-05, API name mistral-medium-2505, Generalist/Premier classification, empty weights array, contextLength 128k, text/image input, text output and function-calling feature. No numeric parameter or active-parameter fields are attached to this entry.

sources.title: Build Agents and Understand Long Docs with Mistral Medium 3 and NVIDIA NIM
sources.evidence: NVIDIA's May 16, 2025 deployment announcement explicitly identifies the original Medium 3 as dense and privately licensed. The article body, independently of its generated summary, describes text/image input, text output, 128K context, multilingual output, instruction following and function calling. NVIDIA is the deployment partner, not the model developer.

sources.title: Magistral — Mistral AI technical report, June 12, 2025
sources.evidence: Mistral's report explicitly identifies Medium 3 as the initial checkpoint for Magistral Medium and calls Magistral its first reasoning models. It studies RL training and weight trajectories, but does not disclose Medium 3 total/active parameters or establish a detailed layer architecture.

sources.title: Model Selection Guide — requested Medium 3 comparison
sources.evidence: Despite the requested retired-model slug, the returned comparison renders current models including Medium 3.5 v26.04. Its 128B total/active entries are labeled Medium 3.5, not Medium 3 v25.05; they cannot be transferred to the audited model.

sources.title: Mistral Medium 3.5 128B official model card
sources.evidence: Later first-party card discloses dense 128B and configurable reasoning specifically for Medium 3.5, naming Medium 3.1 as a predecessor. It provides no exact May 2025 Medium 3 parameter disclosure or statement that the two models share those specifications.

sources.title: Mistral Medium 3 Instruct NVIDIA NIM model card route
sources.evidence: The route returned only the site shell and model title; model-card technical content was unavailable. It was not treated as evidence of any undisclosed specification.

sources.title: Featured models of Foundry model catalog — Mistral-medium-2505 row
sources.evidence: The exact model row documents 128,000-token text input plus images and text output for Microsoft's serving offering. Its tool-calling No conflicts with Mistral's own capability card and describes the provider integration rather than overriding native model support.

sources.title: Mistral Medium 3.0 — Legal Center
sources.evidence: The lifecycle table distinguishes Medium 3.0, 3.1 and 3.5 and dates the base release May 7, 2025. The public page's technical-documentation data says the original model documentation is being prepared for the applicable 2027 deadline; it contains no parameter or architecture details.

sources.title: OpenRouter exact Mistral Medium 3 endpoint metadata
sources.evidence: Live endpoint metadata for mistralai/mistral-medium-3 names Medium 3, gives created=1746627341 (May 7, 2025 UTC), and lists 131072 context for its Mistral provider routes. Tool parameters are listed; no reasoning control is listed. This is primary documentation of OpenRouter's serving routes, not a published native model configuration or inference test.

sources.title: OpenRouter model index — distinct Medium 3, 3.1 and 3.5 entries
sources.evidence: Fresh index read preserves separate mistralai/mistral-medium-3, mistralai/mistral-medium-3.1 and mistralai/mistral-medium-3-5 IDs. Original Medium 3 has a May 7, 2025 creation timestamp and 131072 context, distinguishing this provider record from the separately listed later versions.

name.note: Exact original release name; v25.05 is distinct from Medium 3.1 and 3.5.

developer.note: Mistral AI's own announcement establishes authorship; retain the catalog's normalized developer label.

family.note: Normalized family follows the exact Medium API identifier and Mistral's Medium lifecycle grouping.

release_date.note: Original announcement explicitly makes the API available that day; later partner deployment dates are not the release date.

open_weights.note: Premier/private-license release with no public weights entry. Licensed enterprise self-deployment does not constitute an open-weight release.

license.note: Descriptive license classification follows the explicitly private commercial deployment license. Medium 3.5's Modified MIT license does not apply to this earlier model.

parameters_b.note: No exact production total is disclosed in the inspected release, card, later training report or governance material. Later comparison/card numbers label Medium 3.5 only. Searches also covered exact-name first-party technical and interpretability research; no Medium 3 count disclosure was located. This does not claim an exhaustive proof of absence.

active_parameters_b.note: No separate exact-model active count was found. Do not infer a number from dense architecture or transfer the 128B active entry labeled Medium 3.5.

architecture.note: The original May 2025 deployment partner's announcement explicitly identifies Medium 3 as dense. This establishes the catalog category only; detailed Transformer dimensions were not verified, and no sibling architecture was transferred.

context_window.note: Retain 131072 as explicitly documented OpenRouter hosted-route capacity. The exact Medium 3 name, May 7, 2025 creation date and separate later-version entries support the original v25.05 identity bridge. Mistral publishes nominal 128k; Azure separately documents 128000. These route specifications do not prove a universal native/API enforcement boundary or current backend checkpoint identity.

modalities.note: Exact Mistral model data and original deployment article both explicitly state text/image input and text output. Document-QnA product support is not treated as an additional native modality.

reasoning.note: Mistral calling the subsequent Magistral models its first reasoning models and naming Medium 3 as their initial checkpoint supports an inference that this is an ordinary instruction release, but does not explicitly declare the exact endpoint's native-thinking capability false. Absence of an OpenRouter reasoning parameter is also insufficient. Clear baseline false rather than promote either inference or ordinary reasoning benchmarks to a verified boolean.

tool_call.note: Mistral's exact card/model data and original NVIDIA announcement explicitly support function calling. Microsoft's provider-specific No is not generalized to the model.

description.value: May 2025 proprietary Mistral Medium 3 instruction model with multilingual text, image understanding, coding and native function calling
description.note: Replace generic family wording with exact-release capabilities and avoid implying dedicated thinking support.

patch.description: May 2025 proprietary Mistral Medium 3 instruction model with multilingual text, image understanding, coding and native function calling
patch.notes: Original mistral-medium-2505 release, distinct from Medium 3.1 and 3.5. Total and active parameters remain undisclosed in the inspected exact-model sources. Dense architecture and private licensing are documented by the original NVIDIA deployment announcement. Context 131072 is documented for OpenRouter's original Medium 3 routes; Mistral advertises nominal 128k and Azure separately lists 128000. Exact native enforcement and dedicated-thinking capability are unverified. Route metadata is not an inference test or proof of current backend checkpoint identity.

summary: Audited all 14 fields. Added proprietary licensing and dense architecture and replaced the generic description. Retained 131072 context after directly verifying OpenRouter's original Medium 3 hosted-route disclosure, with nominal Mistral 128k and Azure 128000 distinctions. Cleared reasoning=false because non-dedicated-thinking classification remains an inference rather than explicit exact-endpoint evidence. Confirmed the May 7, 2025 original release, closed weights, text/image input, text output and tools. Total/active parameters remain undisclosed after exact-model release/card, later technical-report, comparison, sibling-card and governance checks. Medium 3.5 counts were excluded; the original NVIDIA model-card route exposed no technical content.
